doc.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012

title: The mystique of jazz's dark side and dying young
summary: Discussion of Bix and the romance of jazz's nocturnal vice, though Weber is substance-free.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I think sometimes the audience in the older days liked the fact that those musicians were going to die young. It’s like let them be that way so we can watch. You know, or then we can tell stories about like Bix Beiderbecke, of course, he’ll live on forever partly because he died so young. And the tragic hero I suppose.

There is the mystique of the dark side, the flirtation with the vice that jazz brings — all the best jazz photography is black and white, smoky club basements, sweaty and guys going “yeah, yeah.” You know there’s this whole feeling of sort of nocturnal and nefarious and sort of, oh — and even here I’m the most substance-free musician there is, but I like going out to a place at three in the morning because there’s something about that life, something about that energy that really attracts me and attracts a lot of people, musicians and non-musicians alike.
